summary: JClaw's runtime guards (CircuitBreaker + LlmResilience, ToolResultVerifier, DangerousActionGate, CompactionGate/ToolResultPruner/TruncationDiagnostics) are all built, tested (CircuitBreakerTest 26 cases, DangerousActionGateTest 31, ToolResultVerifierTest 19, LlmStreamBreakerTest 20) and run by a pre-push hook. Four patterns would let OUR harness catch something it cannot today: (1) a consecutive-death streak breaker inside measure-refute.js so a usage wall stops the fan-out instead of every queued agent launching into it (2026-07-25: all 10 agents died after ~687k tokens; three more wall deaths 08-13/14/15); (2) a reason-carrying death record — measure-refute.js line 192 `.catch(() => null)` discards the error, so a budget-ceiling throw, a wall death and a user skip are one bucket; (3) a structural post-condition on verdicts — a CLEAN with no command run is live today, the exact 'exec exitCode 1 scored a clean pass' blind spot JClaw closed in stage 1.5; (4) a PreToolUse dangerous-command hook — we have NO PreToolUse hook anywhere, run build-loop under bypassPermissions, and SSHD's settings.local.json carries a standing `Bash(rm -rf *)` allow; Claude Code docs confirm an exit-2 hook beats allow rules. A half-open probe before relaunch is ADAPT (one probe, not three). Model fallback and compaction/stubbing are SKIP: the walls that bite are session caps (model-agnostic) and the platform already stubs large tool results behind a file handle (observed this session at 35.4KB).

candidates.pattern: Consecutive-failure streak breaker: after N agent deaths in a row, stop spawning and report the unspawned work as NOT_SPAWNED (fail-closed), rather than letting every queued agent launch into a dead dependency.
candidates.failurePrevented: A usage/credit wall kills agents one after another while the fan-out keeps launching: 2026-07-25 all 10 agents 'failed AFTER burning ~687k tokens' (memory reference-fable5-credits-exhausted.md); 'Three usage-limit deaths in a row on SSHD's L0 lane (08-13, 08-14, 08-15)' (memory project-workflow-salvage-pattern.md). pipeline() has no barrier, so on this 8-CPU box (sysctl hw.ncpu → 8; cap = min(16, cpus-2) = 6) six measure agents launch at once and the remaining units plus every refuter (units × lenses) still queue behind them after the wall hits.

candidates.why: Closes the one wall failure the fail-closed accounting only REPORTS today (it names dead agents but still launches the rest). Streak-of-2 is the whole breaker for a solo run: a rate rule is JClaw's own anti-pattern for low traffic (see antiPatterns).

candidates.pattern: Reason-carrying failure: every breaker transition and every refusal carries WHY (Reason enum with a `manual()` split; ManuallyIsolated vs BreakerOpen), so an operator's stop is never read as the dependency breaking and a diagnosis can be made from the record alone.
candidates.failurePrevented: A dead fan-out whose result cannot say whether the agent hit a usage wall, a budget ceiling, or was skipped by the user — three cases with three different recoveries (wait for reset and resume unedited / narrow the script / nothing to fix). candidates.pattern: Half-open probe: after a trip, admit a bounded number of probes and re-open on the first that fails; close only when all succeed — never relaunch the whole fleet on hope.
candidates.failurePrevented: Relaunching a full fan-out into a wall that has not lifted (three consecutive-day deaths 08-13/14/15 on one lane). Today the advice exists only as prose: memory reference-fable5-credits-exhausted.md:85 'prefer a cheap single-agent probe first if there is any doubt about credit state'; playbooks/crash-resilience.md 'Don't launch a fleet near a limit window' — neither is a mechanism.

candidates.ourEvidence: Prose only (memory line 85; crash-resilience.md). Resume replay is proven — project-workflow-salvage-pattern.md 'resuming unedited replayed 28 agents free' — but pipeline() launches every uncached unit at once (no barrier; concurrency cap 6 here), so the first 6 uncached agents die together on a relaunch into a live wall. grep 'probe' in measure-refute.js and measure-verify.js → 0 hits.
candidates.proposal: measure-refute.js: `args.probeFirst` (default true on any run) — `await spawn(measurePrompt(UNITS[0]))` alone; if it is not a live measurement, return `{ status: 'UNVERIFIED', fatalCount: null, integrity: 'probe unit died; fleet not launched (0 further agents)', units: [...] }`; else run pipeline over UNITS.slice(1) and prepend the probe result. One probe, not JClaw's three: the streak breaker (resilience-gates-1) already re-opens on the next two deaths, and a 3-probe close rule costs 3 serial agents on every healthy run. Test: probe dead → labels.length === 1, status UNVERIFIED.
candidates.doneCriterion: Test PASS/red-first as above; a relaunch into a wall costs exactly ONE agent (visible as 1 label in the journal), not 6.
candidates.cost: ~15 lines + 1 test; adds one agent's wall-clock latency to the front of every run (the probe unit runs alone before the rest start).
candidates.why: Worth having because a wall relaunch has happened three days running, but the latency cost is real on an ADD-friendly workflow, so it is a single probe and an arg, not a 3-permit state machine. Ordering note: adopt after resilience-gates-1, which supplies `spawn()`.

candidates.proposal: agent-harness/hooks/dangerous-gate.sh (≤40 lines, python3 stdin JSON parse, no jq dependency): read `tool_input.command`; if it matches a deny regex — `git push .*(--force|-f)\b`, `git reset --hard`, `git checkout \.`, `git clean`, `--no-verify`, `rm -rf` outside /tmp and the scratchpad, `curl|wget ... antiPatterns.what: A failure-RATE breaker over a rolling window with fleet-sized defaults (window 100, min-calls 20, 50%) — JClaw shipped this first and it never fired for a single operator.
antiPatterns.evidence: commit cea0b21f: "The shipped tuning — a 50% rate over a 100-outcome window, evaluated from 20 calls — is a fleet's. On a single-operator install ... the breaker needed 50 failed turns, about ten hours of hung turns, before it first turned a call away." CircuitBreaker.java:19-23 keeps the rate rule and ADDS the streak.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: Our fan-outs are 10-40 agents per run; a rate rule can never reach min-volume before the run is over. Adopt only the streak (resilience-gates-1) and set it to 2, not 3 — JClaw's own reasoning ('a streak measures the present') applies more strongly the smaller the traffic.

antiPatterns.what: Out-of-band interactive approval (Telegram/Slack approve/deny buttons) that blocks the tool thread for up to 300 s, plus a permissive `allow` default on the trusted origin.
antiPatterns.evidence: DangerousActionGate.java:104 `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300`; :43-47 "blocks the calling (virtual) thread on TelegramApprovalService#await until the user taps a button or the request times out"; :117-118 `CFG_OFF_CHANNEL_POLICY ... DEFAULT_OFF_CHANNEL_POLICY = "allow"`.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: A phone-button approval surface is an interruption channel for a developer with ADD and a second system to maintain on an 8 GB machine; Claude Code's permission prompt + `inputNeededNotifEnabled: true` already is the approval surface. Our gate (resilience-gates-5) is deny-by-regex with exit 2 — no wait, no timeout, and no permissive default.

antiPatterns.what: Stage 2 of tool-result verification: a critic-model pass on every tool return.
antiPatterns.evidence: ToolResultVerifier.java:15-21 "a critic-model pass on every tool return adds roughly one real TTFT per tool round, measured at ~1.5 s against a harness that accounts for 0.2% of a turn ... A check that catches a class of failure for free beats a critic call" — JClaw itself deferred it.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: We already do better: claimcheck resolves every cite deterministically at ±0 in ~0.2 s and the global rule is 'a script beats a swarm ... agents only for what needs reading prose'. An LLM judge per tool result is the swarm-checks-the-script pattern inverted.

antiPatterns.what: A process-wide breaker registry whose config is applied only when a name is first minted, so a later lookup with different tuning silently returns the old breaker.
antiPatterns.evidence: CircuitBreakers.java:15-18 "`config` is applied only when the breaker is first created — a later get with different tuning returns the existing breaker unchanged, so tuning belongs wherever the name is first minted."
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: That is state-schema drift by design (global CLAUDE.md killer #1); acceptable for a long-lived JVM with one owner per name, wrong for us. Our breaker state lives inside one workflow run (a `let` in the script) and dies with it — and the runtime's resume cache already keys on (prompt, opts), so a changed tuning is a changed key, never a stale breaker.

antiPatterns.what: Stubbing large tool results behind a retrieve tool (ccr_retrieve) at the application layer.
antiPatterns.evidence: ToolResultPruner.java:79-83 `stub()` emits 'call ccr_retrieve("<handle>") if you need the full text again'; :33-34 the tool name is a literal to avoid a package cycle.
antiPatterns.whyNotForUs: The Claude Code runtime already persists any tool output over ~35 KB to a file and hands back a preview + path (observed this session); building a second mechanism under it is the speculative abstraction the ship-bar forbids.
